name: Social Insurance (Bảo hiểm xã hội)

references.title: Law 41/2024 arts.31(1)(b), 37(2): use actual qualifying stoppage salary; temporarily suspend compulsory SI during detention/disciplinary suspension, restore arrears when full wages are back-paid. A dated insurance_review supplies an exact monthly base/status; mixed and split months are not guessed.
Law on Social Insurance 41/2024/QH15 (Luật Bảo hiểm xã hội)
references.quote: Art.33–34: 8% employee and 17.5% employer, on a salary capped at 20 times the statutory reference level (2,530,000, ceiling 50,600,000). Employer 17.5% = 3% sickness and maternity + 14% retirement and survivorship + 0.5% occupational accident and disease; 17.3% where the reduced 0.3% occupational-accident rate applies. Above the ceiling the employer’s share is the ceiling at the employer’s own rate. Art.31(1)(đ): tiền lương làm căn cứ đóng thấp nhất bằng mức tham chiếu (2,530,000 đ). Art.33(5): an unpaid month of 14 or more working days is waived for the listed categories (not part-time employees, art.2(1)(l)), and may be continued by agreement at the most recent contribution base (arts.33(5), 34(3)); art.33(6): SI is due in the first working or return month with at least 14 sickness-benefit working days. Art.53(8): birth, adoption under six months, surrogate-birth and commissioning-mother benefit leave are exempt without the 14 working days; other maternity-benefit cases only from 14 working days in the month. Art.2(1)(a): fixed-term contract covered only “từ đủ 01 tháng trở lên”. Art.2(7)(b): a domestic worker is not a compulsory participant. Art.2(2)(b): a foreign employee at retirement age (measured at the contract’s signing) is excluded; also excluded: foreign employee on a contract under 12 months, intra-company transferee, treaty-exempt. Part-time pay below 2,530,000 is outside compulsory SI and UI.

A part-time employee’s base is the pay of the month (art.7(2)). Occupational-accident contributions stay on the compulsory SI salary (art.43(2)).

references.quote: In force 16 May 2026. name: Personal Income Tax (Thuế thu nhập cá nhân)

references.title: Resident salary withholding (Decree 253/2026/NĐ-CP art.46(3)-(4); Circular 111/2013 art.8(2)(b) before; Law 109/2025/QH15 arts.8-9): current-employer year-to-date ordinary and bonus income, employee statutory contributions and tax are read from prior payslips of the same tax year. The annual tariff is the monthly table thresholds × 12. A one-off bonus enters the year-to-date base once; it is never multiplied by the remaining months and is not taxed through the monthly ladder as if it were the recurring salary.
Circular 87/2026/TT-BTC
references.quote: In force 1 July 2026, resident salary from tax period 2026. Its art.6(2) replaces Circular 111/2013/TT-BTC; Circular 111/2013 and Law 04/2007/QH12 apply only where the earlier rule is contrasted.

references.quote: Art.29(2): five-rung monthly scale for salary income from the 2026 tax period (5% to 10,000,000; 10% to 30,000,000; 20% to 60,000,000; 30% to 100,000,000; 35% above). Art.8(2): the employee’s compulsory SI 8% + HI 1.5% (and UI 1% for a citizen) actually charged in the month is deducted. Art.9: annual table for the December finalisation.

references.title: Resolution 110/2025/UBTVQH15
references.quote: From the 2026 tax period: personal deduction 15,500,000 and 6,200,000 per registered dependant a month.

references.title: Decree 253/2026/NĐ-CP
references.quote: Art.4: resident = present 183 days in the calendar year or twelve months from arrival, or registered permanent residence or rented home for 183 days or more; art.5: anyone else is non-resident (20% on taxable remuneration, no personal, dependant or insurance deductions). Neither law nor decree presumes residence, so an unrecorded residence stops the calculation. Art.66(1)(a): residence governs the calendar year, or the first twelve months from arrival; art.46(3), art.64(4): income is taxed when paid, each month on the status recorded for it; a status change is settled in the annual finalisation (art.51), which re-prices wage income on the resident table and credits what was withheld at 20%; earlier months are never re-withheld. Art.26(1): overtime and statutory cessation leave exemptions apply to residents from tax year 2026 and non-residents from 1 July 2026 (art.69); before that non-residents keep the earlier overtime-premium exemption and taxable leave cash-out; a future departure does not establish cessation; payments beyond statutory limits remain taxable. Art.26(2): pay for untaken leave exempt only within Labour Code art.113(3) conditions and rate (Decree 145/2020 art.67(3) day), art.26(3) taxes the excess in the month it is paid (art.46(3)). Art.49 medical, education and charity deductions are settled by the taxpayer with the tax office (art.51(3)). Art.51(2): December finalisation only for an employee who authorised it and qualifies. Art.8(2)(g) with art.69(1)(b): from 1 July 2026 a meal paid by the employer is taxable only above 1,200,000 a month; a meal served in kind is not income. Art.8(2)(h): rent, power and water the employer pays on the worker’s behalf taxable at the amount paid, not above 15% of the worker’s other taxable income at the unit. Art.46(2)(a) with art.69(1)(a): voluntary pension and life insurance deducted as paid, at most 3,000,000 a month including the employer’s share (employer contributions are taxable), from tax year 2026; art.69(1)(a) applies the salary-income rules from tax period 2026, so the December finalisation caps every 2026 month at 3,000,000, January–June included (1,000,000 before July 2026 for the months withheld); art.70(2) settles the months withheld under the old rule in that finalisation (signed text pp.56–57, read 2026-10-08). Art.50(2): a resident with no contract or one under three months is withheld 10% on a payment of 5,000,000 or more; nothing below it or with the commitment form. Art.26(1) exempts “tiền lương, tiền công làm việc ban đêm” — the wage for night work itself.

references.title: Decree 126/2020/NĐ-CP
references.quote: The employer may make the year-end finalisation (December re-pricing on the annual table) only for an employee who authorised it and qualifies.

references.title: Circular 111/2013/TT-BTC

references.quote: Union members in an enterprise outside the State sector pay dues; paid to the union, never by a non-member.

references.title: Decision 61/QĐ-TLĐ of the Vietnam General Confederation of Labour
references.quote: In force from 1 July 2025. A member in an enterprise outside the State sector pays dues of 0.5% of the salary the compulsory social insurance is based on, capped at 10% of the base salary (mức lương cơ sở) — at most 253,000 (10% of 2,530,000). Art.1 waives dues only for a member on SI benefit for a month or more, or without work, income or pay for a month or more — not for the 14 unpaid working days that end the month’s SI contribution (Law 41/2024 art.33(5)); such a member still pays 0.5% of the insurance salary. A member outside compulsory SI pays a set sum of at least 0.5% of the base salary, which the union sets. In a State-owned enterprise the dues are 0.5% of the take-home salary after SI, HI, UI and PIT, same cap. Owner rule 2026-11-04: this version computes State-sector and other members on the compulsory-SI wage base (actual ordinary pay plus fixed allowances), capped at 10% of the base salary; the bonus-inclusive GROSS checkpoint is not a dues base. Caveat (owner rule 2026-09-28, law silent on a part month): the waiver applies to a pay month in which every scheduled working day is wholly unpaid; maternity-benefit months stay waived as SI’s own exemption; a month with SI nil counts as a benefit month only for a birth, adoption, surrogate-birth or commissioning-mother maternity spell, not a paternity spell (at most 14 working days, art.53(2)) or a short maternity event (miscarriage, check-up, contraception).
